entries.title: Torque
entries.content: Torque is rotational force: T = Force × perpendicular distance. Unit N·m (1 kg·m ≈ 9.81 N·m). Motor torque: T = P/ω where ω = 2π×RPM/60. A 1 HP motor at 3000 RPM gives about 2.4 N·m.

entries.title: Gears & Gear Ratio
entries.content: Gears transmit rotation between shafts. Gear ratio = driven teeth / driver teeth. Ratio > 1 reduces speed and multiplies torque (e.g., 20T→40T halves RPM, doubles torque). Types: spur, helical (quiet), bevel (90°), worm (high reduction, self-locking), rack & pinion (rotary→linear).

entries.title: Pulleys & Belts
entries.content: Belt drives connect shafts via pulleys. Speed relation: N1×D1 = N2×D2 (RPM × diameter). A 100mm driver at 1200 RPM with a 200mm driven pulley gives 600 RPM. Belt types: flat, V-belt (most common), timing belt (positive grip, no slip). Belt speed = π×D×N/60.

entries.title: Bearings
entries.content: Bearings reduce friction between rotating parts. Ball bearings: high speed, moderate load (6203, 6205 common codes). Roller/taper: heavy load, radial+axial. Sleeve/bush: cheap, quiet, low speed. Lubrication (grease/oil) is essential — wrong fit or no grease is the top bearing killer.

entries.title: Stress & Strain
entries.content: Stress σ = Force/Area (N/mm² = MPa). Strain ε = extension/original length (dimensionless). Hooke's Law: σ = E×ε, where E = Young's Modulus (steel ~200 GPa, aluminium ~70 GPa). Yield strength = stress where permanent deformation begins; ultimate tensile strength = max before breaking.

entries.title: Hydraulics & Pneumatics
entries.content: Fluid power uses pressurized fluid to do work. Hydraulics: liquid (oil), high force, pressures 70–700 bar, used in JCBs, presses. Pneumatics: air, fast & clean, 6–10 bar, used in automation. Cylinder force F = Pressure × Piston area. Pascal's law: pressure applied to enclosed fluid transmits equally in all directions.
